cases.name: oom_diagnosis
cases.prompt: A Torc job on Slurm exited with 137. Diagnose it.
assertions: identifies 137 as SIGKILL, typically out of memory
checks Slurm state via torc slurm sacct or the dmesg log
recommends raising memory or running torc workflows correct-resources
does not assert OOM from the exit code alone without corroborating evidence

cases.name: orphaned_running_jobs
cases.prompt: Torc shows 12 jobs as running but the Slurm allocation ended hours ago.
assertions: uses torc workflows sync-status with --dry-run first
explains that orphaned jobs are marked failed so recovery can proceed
notes that this clears stale allocations that block torc recover

cases.name: runtime_blocked_packing
cases.prompt: Allocations are running with free CPUs but my ready Torc jobs never start.
assertions: explains that a job whose runtime exceeds remaining walltime will not be started
suggests more allocations, longer walltime, or lower job runtime
does not require Slurm access for the diagnosis

cases.name: missing_logs
cases.prompt: torc results list --include-logs warns that every log file is missing.
assertions: checks that the output directory matches the one used during the run
notes that log filenames embed run_id and attempt_id
considers stdio modes and delete_on_success as intentional suppression
considers that logs may live on the compute node or worker

cases.name: offline_drain_recovery
cases.prompt: The Torc server was down for an hour. Jobs clearly finished but no results exist.
assertions: explains offline drain and the offline_journal directory
runs torc workflows reconcile with the workflow ID and run ID
uses --base-dir when journals are spread across compute nodes
